content: REC8, also known as meiotic recombination protein REC8 homolog, is a protein encoded by the REC8 gene in humans. This protein is a meiosis-specific component of the cohesin complex, which plays a critical role in binding sister chromatids in preparation for the two divisions of meiosis. During meiosis, REC8 is removed from sister chromatids in a sequential manner. In the first meiotic division, REC8 is removed from the arms of chromosomes, facilitating the separation of homologous chromosomes. However, it remains at the centromeres to ensure that sister chromatids stay joined until the anaphase of meiosis II. At this stage, the remaining cohesin is removed, leading to the separation of sister chromatids. The REC8 gene encodes a member of the kleisin family of structural maintenance of chromosome (SMC) protein partners. The REC8 protein localizes to the axial elements of chromosomes during meiosis in both oocytes and spermatocytes. It appears to function in conjunction with other cohesins, such as STAG3, SMC1β, and SMC3, to maintain sister chromatid cohesion throughout the entire meiotic process in human oocytes. In mice, the homologous protein is a key component of the meiotic cohesin complex, which regulates both sister chromatid cohesion and recombination between homologous chromosomes. Multiple alternatively spliced variants of the REC8 gene have been identified, all encoding the same protein. REC8 remains in complex with SMC proteins until anaphase, at which point it is degraded by the enzyme separase. This degradation occurs only after the spindle assembly checkpoint has been bypassed. Unlike other members of the kleisin family, such as SCC1, REC8 must be phosphorylated before it can be degraded. Prior to anaphase, REC8 is protected from phosphorylation by Protein Phosphatase 2 (PP2A-B56) in mice. PP2A is recruited to the cohesin complex by Shugoshin 2 (Sgo2, or SGOL2 in yeast). Once the spindle assembly checkpoint is bypassed, separase becomes activated and degrades phosphorylated REC8. This untethers cohesin from sister chromatids, allowing for the segregation of chromosomes. REC8 has been shown to interact with SMC3, further highlighting its role in the cohesin complex and its importance in meiotic chromosomal dynamics.
